runtimeEvidence.interpretation: Fail-closed behavior was correct. The candidate exposed that the template projector invented absent enhancement fields, reference provenance polluted validation identity, and unresolved multi-enchant source values required explicit partial classification.
Aggregate diagnostics proved all 100 remaining conflicts differed only by finger1/finger2 or trinket1/trinket2 placement; static facts and serializer inputs matched exactly.
The transaction rolled back because a partial reference used an empty string instead of SQL NULL for its optional exact-instance foreign key.
The transaction rolled back during exact read-back because psycopg had already decoded a scalar JSON context. Store SELECTs now cast every JSONB value to canonical text before parsing.

The candidate and deployed-runtime rerun both pass with the same registry/report identities. Partial multi-enchant source rows remain explicit and have no exact key; future loadout consumers are verified-reference-only.

risks.detail: No verified reference has an enhancement mismatch. Fifty-five source rows contain multiple unresolved enchant values and remain explicit partial references without ExactItemInstance keys.
The production snapshot currently contains zero structured personal gear templates; projector/store tests pass and recursive inspection finds zero owner-bearing keys in all 1242 sealed references.
Only 1242 referenced source rows were considered and 749 exact identities were materialized; 47313 unreferenced historical rows were not copied. Runtime stayed below both hard limits.
Every blocked and passing candidate retained generation 32; services stayed active with zero restarts.

The production Phase 1 Catalog table is owned by the database administrator, so the repository migration was applied idempotently through the existing PostgreSQL administrator path after the narrower runtime roles correctly failed to create cross-table foreign keys.
